questions.question: Which HTTP method is meant for creating a new item, where the server chooses the new id?
questions.explanation: POST creates a new item. PUT replaces an item at a known address, and GET only reads.

questions.question: @GetMapping("/orders") is a shortcut for which annotation?
questions.explanation: @GetMapping is @RequestMapping with the method already set to GET.

questions.question: A method annotated @DeleteMapping("/{id}") and @ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.NO_CONTENT) removes an order successfully. What does the client receive?
questions.explanation: NO_CONTENT is 204, which means the delete worked and there is nothing to send back.

questions.question: Only @GetMapping("/menu") exists. A client sends POST /menu. What status does it get?
questions.explanation: The address exists but has no POST method, so Spring answers 405 Method Not Allowed.

questions.question: A developer writes @GetMapping("/cancel/{id}") and removes an order inside it. Why is this a problem?
options: GET must never change data, since browsers and crawlers may call it on their own
Path variables are not allowed with GET
Spring refuses to start with a GET that deletes data
Records cannot be removed from a map
questions.explanation: GET should only read. Use @DeleteMapping so a stray link visit or crawler cannot remove data.
